requirement:
The harness MUST record the sources it supplies to the model, including
mandatory inputs, additional reads, and selected search dependencies under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.finish_search.inputs`, using the evidence input formats
defined by {cite}`requirements.ci.outline_inputs`,
{cite}`requirements.ci.requirements_inputs`, and
{cite}`requirements.definitions.inputs`. The harness MUST create these records
itself so ordinary evidence validation can check them later. For citation assessments, additional node reads and selected excerpts are recorded as SDK dependencies under {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.search.finish_search.inputs` and {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.validation-context.read_node.inputs`.
rationale:
I found no test-adequacy gap in the reviewed tests for `requirements.authoring.delivered_inputs`. The mapping below covers each obligation.

**Mandatory inputs are recorded in the evidence input formats**
- `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[ollama_cli_delivers_sources_records_fixme_and_keeps_usage_content_free]` checks the outline input for `src/lib.rs` `fn[ready_test]`. It also checks the definition input `terms.readiness`. Every outline input must carry `hash`, and none may carry source text.
- `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[stdout_emits_only_evidence_json_without_changing_project_files]` checks all three input forms in the emitted record:
  - the requirements input (`input["requirements"] == SUBJECT`),
  - the definition input,
  - the outline input.
- It also checks that outline inputs have exactly the keys `file`, `hash` and `item`. It runs six determination and verbosity combinations.

**Additional reads are recorded, deduplicated, and limited to successful deliveries**
- The ollama test makes a repeated `read_node` of `extra.txt` and checks that the record equals `outline_inputs_for_lines` exactly, so the repeat is recorded once.
- A failed read of `absent.txt` is not recorded.
- A `list_sources` listing is not recorded.
- `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[implementation_discovery_has_no_text_or_evidence_until_the_model_requests_a_read]` shows that `outgoing_edges` discovery supplies no text and no inputs. After the model reads `fn[ready]`, the input is recorded exactly once.
- `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[optional_requirement_and_example_reads_preserve_the_complete_declarations]` reads an optional requirement and an optional example. The record contains the exact requirements-input form: `requirements`, `matches`, and the full raw declaration lines. Editing a declaration afterwards makes `validate_repository` report the subject and `requirements.illustration`.

**Selected search dependencies are recorded; unselected ones are not**
- `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[relying_on_a_helper_excerpt_makes_edits_to_that_helper_stale]` selects a `search_text` excerpt with `finish_search`. The helper's outline input is recorded, an unselected hit (`fn[unselected]`) is not, and an explicit read is recorded too.
- That test edits the file after delivery, and validation then reports the changed hash for `fn[assert_refusal]`. This confirms the harness records the delivered snapshot.
- The ollama test shows that a search which selects nothing records nothing.
- `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/project_sources.rs#mod[tests]/fn[search_obligations_follow_delivery_and_keep_the_original_snapshot]` checks the SDK side:
  - empty `used` adds no dependency;
  - a repeated selection yields the same original dependency;
  - a later page's selection records that page's node;
  - invalid calls record nothing;
  - the original fingerprint survives a later source change.

**The harness creates the records itself so ordinary evidence validation can check them**
- The ollama test runs `habeas::validate_repository` on the harness-written evidence and finds no error for that evidence file.
- The helper-staleness and optional-reads tests show validation detecting later edits.

**Citation assessments record reads and selected excerpts as SDK dependencies**
- `src/authoring/mod.rs#mod[tests]/fn[citation_and_example_assessments_record_selected_and_explicit_reads]` runs a citation subject and an example subject. A selected search excerpt (`fn[first]`), an explicit read (`fn[second]`) and an optional definition read (`terms.unused`, with its exact text) are all recorded. An untouched function (`fn[untouched]`) is not.
- `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/tests.rs#fn[graph_tools_record_delivered_snapshots_and_prepared_pages_do_not_record_delivery]` checks delivery-time recording through the SDK. Dependencies are recorded only after a successful provider exchange. A failed exchange records nothing, except for a direct context read. Prepared but undelivered pages record nothing.

**Other tests**
- `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[bedrock_cli_uses_selected_profile_region_and_converse_tools]` repeats the read-recording check for the Bedrock backend.
- `tests/live_bedrock.rs#fn[live_bedrock_authoring]` checks that a read source appears as an outline input without text.

Every obligation has a test with relevant assertions, and every test carries a `{test}` marker for the subject. I found no marking gap and no missing scenario.

text: :::{req} delivered_inputs
The harness MUST record the sources it supplies to the model, including
mandatory inputs, additional reads, and selected search dependencies under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.finish_search.inputs`, using the evidence input formats
defined by {cite}`requirements.ci.outline_inputs`,
{cite}`requirements.ci.requirements_inputs`, and
{cite}`requirements.definitions.inputs`. The harness MUST create these records

itself so ordinary evidence validation can check them later. For citation assessments, additional node reads and selected excerpts are recorded as SDK dependencies under {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.search.finish_search.inputs` and {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.validation-context.read_node.inputs`.
:::{req} finish_search.inputs

Habeas MUST store the source dependencies selected by `finish_search` under {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.search.finish_search.inputs` as outline inputs under {cite}`requirements.ci.outline_inputs`. Each input identifies the file, selector, and structural hash from the snapshot that supplied the selected excerpt.
:::{req} outline_inputs
For an outline input, Habeas MUST parse `file` with its language's grammar under
{cite}`requirements.references.outlines` and resolve `item` to exactly one
outline node under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors`. It MUST
compare `hash` with the node's current structural hash under
{cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`. For display and reference coverage, it MUST derive the inclusive line range
from the first and last bytes of the SDK outline item's attachment-inclusive
span under {cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.attachments.item_span`. An empty
span covers the line at its start. Moving the node, editing other
nodes, or editing comments its profile does not hash MUST NOT invalidate the
input. Habeas MUST report a missing file, parse failure,
invalid or ambiguous selector, or changed hash.
:::{req} requirements_inputs

For a requirements input, `requirements` MUST be a {term}`requirements.references.definition_selection`, and Habeas MUST match it against all defined requirements and named examples. It MUST recompute the matches during validation, sort their full names, and compare them with `matches`. It MUST take each match's complete raw fenced declaration, including its opening and closing lines, concatenate those declarations in full-name order with one blank line between them, and compare the resulting raw lines with `text`. It MUST retain every match's current source file and inclusive line range for display and reference coverage. A selection matching no definitions MUST be invalid. Adding, removing, renaming, or changing a matched definition MUST invalidate the stored input; moving an unchanged declaration within the book MUST NOT. Errors MUST identify the selection and affected definitions when available.
:::{req} inputs

Evidence inputs MAY have a definition form containing exactly `definition` and `text`. `definition` MUST identify one named definition; `text` MUST contain its complete raw fenced declaration as source lines, including its phrase option and explanatory body.

Validation MUST reject missing definitions and changed snapshot text, identifying the definition and showing a compact diff when available. Moving an unchanged definition within its chapter MUST NOT invalidate its snapshot. Evidence displays MUST show the definition name, current source location, and recorded text.
:::{req} finish_search.inputs
For each selected tag, the harness records the node identity and fingerprint
from the snapshot that produced the delivered excerpt. If the excerpt also shows source owned by other outline nodes, record those nodes’ read fingerprints as well. Selecting a tag again
preserves the original dependency. Earlier selections survive later calls.
An empty `used` list adds no dependency. Unselected excerpts and the match set
add none either. An invalid call leaves all recorded inputs intact.
:::{req} read_node.inputs
A successful `ValidationContext::read` records the node's identity and the
fingerprint of the returned contents, under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.evidence.node_inputs`. A failed read records no
successful observation. The evidence becomes stale when a later read of that
node has a different fingerprint; a failure to resolve it is reported by
{cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.evidence.checking_records`.
For a Rust caller, the SDK records the fingerprint when `read` returns the
contents. For an agent, the harness puts a tool result in the next request to
the model and records the fingerprint once the provider responds successfully.
That successful exchange is *delivery*. For example, suppose the tool reads a
function that returns `3`, and someone changes it to return `4` before the
provider responds. The model saw the version that returns `3`, so the SDK
records the fingerprint it computed from that version. Reading the function
again at this point would record a fingerprint for code the model never saw.
:::{definition} definition_selection
:phrase: definition selection
A full requirement or example name, or a definition glob, identifying the
requirements and named examples it matches under
{cite}`requirements.references.definition_globs`. A name without `*` selects
exactly that definition.
